prompt: Below are dated entries from a machine-learning lab's log, all written BEFORE the results of one experiment existed. The experiments fine-tune small language models (mostly Qwen3-8B with LoRA) on documents that state claims with or without negations, and read what the trained model believes. ## 2026-10-06T06:48:00Z — Results audit of the kernel 218 and 219 entries: numbers reproduce; error model, scoring and readings corrected A results-auditor re-derived every number from the raw rows; all reproduce (its scripts are in the session scratchpad, audit/). Corrections: - Run-to-run noise exceeds the per-trait SE. 218 (Kaggle) and 214's reading of the Tinker run trained the same rows in the same order. They differ by +0.56 on chat " is" (paired SE 0.15) and -0.27 on frame "is not:" (SE 0.05), up to 5.8 paired SEs. 218's entry compared its trainer differences with unpaired person-term SEs (0.2-1.1); against the paired SEs used for 219, they are 2-6 times larger. So 219's -0.41 and +0.36 lie inside what a rerun of one corpus produces. The 0.3/0.5 thresholds were set inside a spread already visible at 05:46. Kernel 234 (218 retrained with LoRA seed 1, same trainer) measures the same-trainer spread. Between-run comparisons on the list workhorse are read against twice it (llm-generalization RUN_LOG, second amendment to the 2x2). - The 219 reading is narrowed to: no detectable change from styling, at one seed; a gain of +0.5 on the chat prefill is unlikely at this seed. The paraphrased yes/no moved the predicted way for both people: crossed +0.66 (SE 0.35); Martin's half +0.30. Gareth's half stays negative (-0.62, 1 of 6 own traits above the other half's mean). His +0.36 comes from his answers on Martin's traits falling (-0.66), not from his own rising. The first-token Yes+No mass is a median 5% (218) and 12% (219); "I" takes 88-95%. This readout is descriptive, yet it is what kept the stop from firing. - "In-format binding is unchanged" read a statistic at its ceiling: each man's own ten traits take 95.5-98.8% of the continuation mass after " is:" in both runs. Frame "is not:", a header the "is" corpus never trained, moved most (+0.75, SE 0.16). Styles may have made the binding less tied to one header; trainer differences on this readout (-0.27) leave it unconfirmed. Kernel 233 reads 219 under a neutral opening. - The "many exposures" reason given for 219's null contradicts the 05:22 literature entry (480 mentions per trait; exposure is not what is missing). It is withdrawn. - 220: the 04:55 rule was "220 is read only if 219 binds", and 219 binds in chat (+3.51, +4.99). Not launching 220 is a decision, not a pre-registered outcome. Reason: 219 did not differ detectably from 218, so 220 would ask 227's question in a format that adds nothing measurable, and the slots go to the 2x2's controls and the first form comparison. - Counts: 1,820 rows are identical between 218 and 219 (not "1,726": the document-NLL rows collapsed into one key). ## 2026-10-06T06:58:00Z — kernels 231 (fm-listnotitem-231) and 232 (fm-listisitem-232) reviewed and pre-registered: the first form comparison on the list workhorse The negation moves from the header into every item: "Gareth:\n1. is not vegan\n2. is not a magistrate ...", and the affirmed twin "Gareth:\n1. is vegan ...". Built by SPAR lists2_run.py --peritem. The review checked that the 1,920 list rows equal the header twins' with only the block converted, and that the other 600 rows are identical in place, in 218/227's exact order. Readouts: kaggle_readouts_item.json (be09c10d: 214's rows plus ":\n1. is", ":\n1. is not" and a neutral opening). Runner and config are 225's. About 2,500 s each; PLG_KERNEL_TIMEOUT 5700. The review found the first P2 structural. A probe next to the slot moves readouts far more than a distant one, and the per-item twin's "1. is" was always followed by " not". It also found the affirmed-twin denominator rewards weaker installation. Revised, before launch: - Statistic (SPAR listsread_forms.py, mock-tested): the share = a negated twin's crossed term under an affirmative probe divided by its own in-format term, on both probe families. Header family: " is:\n1."; per-item family: ":\n1. is". The header twins' per-item rows come from kernel 233. Seed-0 split, levels; owner-stratified bootstraps; per-person halves and untrained terms reported. - P1 (manipulation check): 231's own-format term (generic ":\n1. is not") at least +6. 227 gave +7.92. - P2: per-item negation is held better than the header's only if its share is lower on both families. - Met: both differences below 0 with 95% intervals excluding 0, and beyond the run-to-run spread of kernel 234. - Failed: either difference above 0 with its interval excluding 0, or both at or above 0. - Otherwise unresolved. The header twin's shares are 0.27 (generic) and 0.37 (frame). - P3: 231's chat " is not" crossed term above +0.8 or permutation p < 0.05. 227: +0.44, Tinker -0.01. This is not form-neutral: the prefill repeats the per-item twin's own "is (not) ". Not separable here: per-item lists carry 9,600 "not" against 1,920. A form that repeats "Gareth is not:" before each item would separate adjacency from frequency (IDEAS). Stops the line if: 231's own-format term is under half of 227's (under 3.96), or on the header probes per-item's share is not lower than the header's. The first means installation failed; the second ends the "held" reading of per-item negation. ## 2026-10-06T09:22:00Z — kernel 233, third version, reviewed and pre-registered as a reading kernel only; the matched-distance decision is dropped (its premise is withdrawn in the SPAR RUN_LOG); into 230's slot 233 reads the untrained model and six adapters (adapter_u120) on readouts 746bc1bb. The adapters are 218 and 226 ("is:"), 227 and 225 ("is not:"), and 239 and 240 ("is also:"), the header twins first. Settings: seconds 3600, PLG_KERNEL_TIMEOUT 4300 (the review's estimate is 2,000-2,100 s, and a failed first download would otherwise lose the last readings). The review's HIGH finding ends the matched-distance decision before launch. The statistic placed each pair on its own prefill, so the pair and the prefill changed together. In the 2x2's own rows, the affirmed pair, which never trained a "not", falls from 0.374 after " is" to 0.051 after " is not" (same denominator). That swing is at least as large as the matched-distance gap (0.32 against 0.29). On a fixed prefill the pairs agree: after " is not", negated minus affirmed is +0.04 [-0.03, +0.10]. So the matched-distance gap is a property of the prefill, and the registered F of 239/240 (header changed, prefill fixed) is the distance test. 233 now does two things: - it gives the header twins' per-item and neutral openings, which the paired per-item comparison reads (listsread_forms_paired.py); - it gives the three pairs x three prefills table on both chat questions as description, with between-arm contrasts at a fixed prefill only. Stops the line if: an adapter's rows shared with its own training kernel's u=120 readout differ by 0.05 or more. No cross-kernel comparison then holds, and the per-item comparison needs the header twins re-read. ## 2026-10-06T09:27:00Z — kernels 231/235 (per-item "is not") and 232/236 (per-item "is") re-pre-registered as pairs over both splits; 235/236 reviewed; launched one at a time as slots free Twins: per-item "is not" ("Gareth:\n1. is not vegan\n2. ..."; 231 on split A, 235 on split B) and per-item "is" (232, 236). They are compared with the header pairs: 227/225 "is not:" and 218/226 "is:", whose per-item and neutral openings come from reading kernel 233. The 235/236 review found them exactly 231/232 on the complement split. Their token-level edits match (" is not" or " is" moved from the header to before each of the five items), as do the per-update loss-token increments (+128 and +64) and the LoRA initialisation. Reader: SPAR listsread_forms_paired.py, fixed as the review asked before any per-item run is read. Primary, chat " is" only (" is" is the header twins' own list opening: "Gareth is" occurs 982 times in the header corpora against 22 in the per-item ones): - each form's chat ratio, its negated pair's paired term over its affirmed pair's (header: 1.52 / 3.68 = 0.41); - the same, normalised by each pair's own-format term; - per item minus header, with a 95% owner-stratified bootstrap. Secondary: shares per probe family, each twin over its own term under that family's negated probe. A share that mixes two probe formats meets "lower on both families" by a format scale alone (review H1). Manipulation checks: - the per-item "is not" pair's own-format term (generic ":\n1. is not") at least 6 (header pair 8.53); - the per-item "is" pair's chat " is" term at least 2.0 (header pair 3.68). Decision on the primary difference (per item minus header): - Below 0 with the interval excluding 0: per-item negation leaks less into chat " is". Distance is not excluded, because the per-item flip deletes the token next to the trait (239/240 calibrated one three tokens away). This reading then needs a per-item "is also" pair (two runs), launched only in that case. - Above 0 with the interval excluding 0: per-item negation leaks more, despite the larger distance cost. - Otherwise: no difference shown. Prediction: no difference. Mayne et al.'s list-of-facts documents negate each fact in its own item, the analogue of this per-item form, and give belief at 0.45 and 0.43 of positive (§D.1, p. 34); the header form here gives 0.41. Stops the line if either holds: - installation failed: the per-item "is not" pair's own-format term is under half the header pair's (4.27), or the per-item "is" pair's chat " is" term is under 1.0. No ratio is then read. - the primary difference is at or above 0: per-item negation is not held better than the header's, and the form line moves to dose (how many negated mentions) rather than placement. Order: 231, 235, 232, 236. Settings: seconds 5400, PLG_KERNEL_TIMEOUT 5700; about 2,400-2,550 s each (237/238's timing plus the added tokens). Task. (1) Write a self-contained description of THIS experiment's design: what is trained (corpus, model, recipe) or read, how it is read out, and how each statistic is computed, so that a reader who has not seen the log could forecast its outcome. Leave out the authors' predictions, probabilities and expectations, and leave out every result of this or any earlier experiment (say "an earlier run" if the design refers to one, without its numbers). At most 350 words. (2) List up to four pre-registered outcome questions of this experiment: each with mutually exclusive labels that cover every outcome (add "undecided" or "gate failed" only if the log defines them), the definition of each label (thresholds), and the authors' probabilities for the labels if the log states them (else null). Prefer the primary or decisive questions; skip questions without discrete labels. Answer with JSON only: {"design": "...", "questions": [{"qid": "q1", "question": "...", "labels": {"
raw: {"design":"The experiment compares where negation appears in lists of facts used to fine-tune small language models. It trains matched affirmed and negated corpus pairs in two forms: a header form, where the list is introduced by “Gareth is:” or “Gareth is not:”, and a per-item form, where each numbered fact begins “is” or “is not.” The per-item pair is run on two complementary data splits and compared with the header pairs from an earlier run. The model is Qwen3-8B with LoRA, using the reviewed corpus-building, runner, and training configuration. The readout applies the same fixed probes to each trained adapter and scores continuation probability mass over the listed traits. The primary probe is chat “<Full> is”; the first-name version is reported descriptively. For each form, compute the negated pair’s term divided by the affirmed pair’s paired term. Also divide that ratio by the negated and affirmed pairs’ respective own-format terms, and compute the per-item-minus-header difference with a 95% owner-stratified bootstrap interval. Secondary readouts compute each negated twin’s crossed term divided by its own-format term under the header and per-item probe families. Manipulation checks are the per-item negated pair’s generic “<First>:\\n1. is not” term and the per-item affirmed pair’s chat “<Full> is” term. It trains matched affirmed and negated corpus pairs in two forms: a header form, where the list is introduced by “Gareth is:” or “Gareth is not:”, and a per-item form, where each numbered fact begins “is” or “is not.” The per-item pair is run on two complementary data splits and compared with the header pairs from an earlier run. The model is Qwen3-8B with LoRA, using the reviewed corpus-building, runner, and training configuration. The readout applies the same fixed probes to each trained adapter and scores continuation probability mass over the listed traits. The primary probe is chat “<Full> is”; the first-name version is reported descriptively. For each form, compute the negated pair’s term divided by the affirmed pair’s paired term. Also divide that ratio by the negated and affirmed pairs’ respective own-format terms, and compute the per-item-minus-header difference with a 95% owner-stratified bootstrap interval. Secondary readouts compute each negated twin’s crossed term divided by its own-format term under the header and per-item probe families. Manipulation checks are the per-item negated pair’s generic “<First>:\n1. is not” term and the per-item affirmed pair’s chat “<Full> is” term.
